elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Inserted subparagraph: "Upon written notice to the Terminal Parties, the Terminal Station Right of Use granted to a Party under Subparagraph 11.1 shall extend to that Party's Affiliates, Subsidiaries and Parent Company, on the same terms and conditions." The naming of Subsidiaries and Parent Company alongside the defined "Affiliate" reaches affiliates in the playbook sense.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither 11.1, 11.5 nor the inserted sentence mentions contractors, subcontractors or other persons acting on a Party's behalf; the grant runs only to the Parties, IRU purchasers and now Affiliates/Subsidiaries/Parent Company.

11.1 expressly limits duration: the Terminal Station Right of Use "shall commence on the RFS Date and shall continue for the duration of this Agreement" — a term right, not perpetual, and no paid-up/perpetual concept was added.

The grant contains no "irrevocable" language; it is granted "on the terms and conditions stated in this Paragraph 11" and expires with the Agreement. (No at-will revocation right in favour of the Terminal Parties appears either, but express irrevocability is absent.)

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: The right of use is coterminous with the Agreement ("shall continue for the duration of this Agreement") and nothing in the rendered language ties loss of the right of use to uncured material breach only; the condition is not clearly inapplicable because this is a term (non-paid-up, non-perpetual) right.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: 22.3: "A Party may at any time assign, sell or transfer the whole of its rights and obligations under this Agreement to: (a) a successor of that Party" — no counterparty consent required, and the rights transferred include the Paragraph 11 right of use.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: Inserted subparagraph conditions extension on "written notice to the Terminal Parties" and extends the 11.1 Terminal Station Right of Use to a Party's Affiliates, Subsidiaries and Parent Company on the same terms.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: 22.3(a) permits a Party "at any time" to "assign, sell or transfer the whole of its rights and obligations under this Agreement" to "a successor of that Party", with no consent gate — which captures a successor arising from a merger or acquisition; retained language, no edit needed.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted subparagraph supplies written-notice affiliate coverage of the Terminal Station Right of Use, and successor transfer already exists in retained Subparagraph 22.3(a), so the finding is correctly pitched at the fallback and the redline is position-complete.

Preferred level remains incomplete (no contractor coverage, no perpetual/irrevocable paid-up grant, no termination-only-for-uncured-material-breach limit), which is consistent with the stated decision not to pursue the preferred position.

Minimality holds: one concise insertion, no deletions, no duplication of the existing 22.3(a) successor mechanic, and no extras such as survival tails or expense language. Naming Subsidiaries and Parent Company is justified only because the contract's "Affiliate" definition is narrow; the definition was not supplied for verification, so confirm it before filing — if "Affiliate" already reaches parents and subsidiaries, delete the surplus nouns to avoid duplicate coverage.

Intent preserved: 11.1's duration, 11.5's IRU grant, the Paragraph 11 terms and conditions and the Paragraph 22 assignment mechanics all survive without contradiction, and the extension is expressly "on the same terms and conditions" as the underlying grant.

Drafting check: verify that "Subsidiaries" and "Parent Company" are defined terms in the Agreement's definitions paragraph; if they are not, replace them with descriptive wording so the insertion does not introduce undefined terms.

If the preferred position is later pursued, the exact repairs are: add "and contractors acting on its behalf" to the grant, add express perpetual/irrevocable wording for any paid-up element, and limit revocation of the right of use to uncured material breach.
